anomalies.reason: Same (tenant_id, event_id) as line 2 with an identical payload, received 7.428 s after the first copy: a redelivery, not a second event.
anomalies.proposed_treatment: Idempotent write keyed on (tenant_id, event_id): keep the first copy, count the dropped copy per tenant. The dedup window must outlive SDK retries and any stream rewind.
anomalies.false_positive_risk: An SDK that reuses an id for different events would lose data, which is why payloads are compared before a copy is dropped (see event_id_collision).

anomalies.reason: Personal data in free-form properties: properties.contact_email (email), properties.phone (phone). Values are withheld from this report.
anomalies.proposed_treatment: Field-level policy at the gate: tokenise (keyed hash per tenant) or drop according to the tenant's allow-list before the event reaches logs, metric labels, dashboards or exports. Logs carry event_id and tenant only. This report prints field names, never values.
anomalies.false_positive_risk: Test or role addresses, e-mails inside URLs, order numbers that look like phone numbers. The opposite error matters more: names and free text that no pattern can see.

anomalies.reason: Payload shape differs from the canonical event: top-level key 'timestamp' used for 'ts'; type 'pageview' used for 'page_view'; property 'page_path' used for 'path'; property 'ref' used for 'referrer'; key 'received_at' absent.
anomalies.proposed_treatment: Accept and normalise through a versioned alias map, keep the original payload, count events per tenant and variant. The SDK cannot change, so the pipeline adapts. A missing received_at is stamped at the new edge.
anomalies.false_positive_risk: An alias map can mis-map a tenant's own custom property that happens to share a legacy name. Aliases must be tied to known SDK versions.

anomalies.reason: tenant_id is null or absent: the record cannot be attributed to a customer.
anomalies.proposed_treatment: Quarantine. In the target design the edge derives the tenant from the SDK write key, never from the payload, and a payload tenant that disagrees is quarantined too.
anomalies.false_positive_risk: None for the detection. Any attempt to guess the tenant can leak one customer's visitors into another customer's dashboard.

anomalies.reason: Line 21 is not valid JSON (JSONDecodeError at column 227). Appending one closing brace makes it parse, which shows the record was cut, not what was lost.
anomalies.proposed_treatment: Quarantine the raw bytes with a reason code and count them. The consumer acknowledges the record and moves on: one poison record must never block a shard.
anomalies.false_positive_risk: None for the detection. The risk sits in the remedy: a cut record can be made to parse, but the fields that were cut off are unknown.

anomalies.reason: Received 7.56 s after its client timestamp.
anomalies.proposed_treatment: Accept. Aggregates and segments must be updatable after the fact, and freshness is measured from received_at: no pipeline can show an event within 5 s of a client time that is already older than that on arrival.
anomalies.false_positive_risk: A client clock running behind looks exactly like a late delivery. The SDK sends no sent_at stamp to tell them apart.

anomalies.reason: A delete_all_data message (GDPR claimed) for user u-1077, visitor anon-77a, tenant t-088 travels in the behavioural stream. 1 other record(s) in this file belong to the subject: evt-0006. A delete keyed on user_id alone would miss evt-0006 (anonymous at the time). A delete bounded by client time would miss evt-0006, whose client ts is later than the request although it was received earlier.
anomalies.proposed_treatment: Route to the privacy queue, never to dashboards. Suppress the subject at once (reversible), verify the request with the tenant (the controller) through an authenticated channel, then delete by identity closure inside the tenant, bounded by server receipt time, and record a tombstone that every replay consults.
anomalies.false_positive_risk: The message type is unambiguous. Its authenticity is not: the SDK endpoint is public, so anyone can post this event with any user id.

anomalies.reason: Property count_today=3 is a counter computed by the browser. Before this record the file holds 1 deduplicated page view(s) of /pricing for the same visitor (evt-0001). Counting every line that mentions /pricing, duplicates included, gives 3 (evt-0001, evt-0002, evt-0002).
anomalies.proposed_treatment: Store the property, never use it as segment truth. Segments are computed server-side from deduplicated, automation-filtered events, with 'today' defined by the tenant's time zone.
anomalies.false_positive_risk: The snapshot does not show earlier activity, so the client number may be right. That is the reason to recompute it rather than assume either way.

do_not_act_at_face_value.why: Do not auto-repair a truncated record and let it drive segments or billing: what was lost is unknown.
Do not infer the tenant from the path, from neighbouring lines or from a default bucket.
Do not repair the client timestamp by subtracting a guessed offset. Use the server receipt time and keep the original value.
Do not use contact details found in properties to identify or contact the visitor: they are form input, may belong to someone else, and consent is unknown.
Do not block or delete on the referrer name: it is client-supplied, trivially changed, and the scanner may belong to the tenant. The timing is the evidence.
Do not execute a deletion that arrived on the public event endpoint without verification, and never read 'delete all data' as tenant-wide.
Do not fire a behaviour-based personalization from a counter the browser reports about itself.

watermark_simulation.method: single partition, file order, watermark = max event time seen minus 5 s, no allowed lateness

sample_caveats: 25 lines of seeded synthetic data: the shares of duplicates, automation or malformed records in this file are not estimates of production rates.
The file is a snapshot that starts at 2026-06-15T14:02:11.104Z: counters, identity links and anything defined over 'today' cannot be checked against earlier activity.
Request metadata (write key, IP, user agent, Origin) is absent, so tenant recovery and the stronger automation checks cannot run here.
